data.text: Make a research of how ddflow can manage project specifications, do a deep research and check what we have, what we plan, what could be reused and make a proposition with phase and tasks with dependencies and waves for the gaps

data.note: write the specs research doc and file the phase

data.body:
Ask the operator and file the decision document. Recommended defaults (research sections 6-8): (1) ONE kind `spec` (a data kind, ddflow/templates/kinds/spec.toml) with `class` = feature|design|interface|acceptance; SDD-model's spec-source and CN-spec-kind become instances of it (fields `format` and `source`), not two more kinds; prose stays in a file (docs/specs/<slug>.md, document type `spec`), the record holds metadata, lifecycle and the content digest. ADRs stay decisions. (2) lifecycle draft -> in_review -> approved -> implemented -> verified, plus superseded and withdrawn; implemented/verified are COMPUTED from linked tasks and checks, never set by hand. (3) versioning: the record history plus the content digest at every transition; a named baseline (set of (spec, version, digest)) is the PD-baseline/CN-baseline engine; an approved spec is edited by a new revision that goes through review again, or superseded. (4) approval: a person approves feature/design/acceptance specs; an interface spec whose checks pass may be agent-approved (the D-constellation (4) reading), every approval an event with the approver and the checks; the author's model family may not be the only reviewer (cross-family review). (5) injection: no always-on charter for specs; at claim the SECTIONS of the specs the task cites or whose scope globs it touches, [specs].claim_tokens default 600; `spec show --section` on demand; imported spec text is fenced and trust=imported. (6) drift policy: warn by default (digest changed since claim, spec newer than the code it governs, code changed under an approved spec's scope with no spec change), block per spec or per project as a knob. (7) the `specs` gate is added only where an approved spec's scope matches the item. List every [specs] knob the later tasks read (SPEC-surfaces declares the section).

ACCEPTANCE: docs/ddflow/decisions/specs.md exists, decisions are recorded with --globs, the operator's answers are quoted.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12; shipped defaults overridable per project and org; extend the shared engines instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/project-specifications.md (SPEC-research).
